name: Boa Resposta
tagline: A Portuguese-language AI helper that turns an incoming message into a polished reply.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a prompt with a text box in front of it. The hard parts of reply drafting, understanding tone and producing fluent Portuguese, already live inside the model you would call anyway, not inside the product. A coding agent can give you a local page with a paste box, a tone picker, a few saved context presets and a history list in a single session, and the output quality will be roughly whatever the underlying model gives. What you are really buying from the paid version is someone else's prompt tuning and the fact that it works on your phone without you touching a terminal. If you send dozens of replies a day from a phone, that convenience is worth real money; if you send a few a week from a laptop, it is not.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you paste an incoming message, pick a tone and a saved context preset, and get two or three draft replies you can copy.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic) in .env
Node 20+ and somewhere to run it locally
Willingness to write your own tone and context prompts
whatYouLose: Prompt tuning that someone has already iterated on with real Portuguese users
A phone-friendly experience you did not have to build or deploy
Any sense of per-reply cost control: you now pay the API directly
Whatever templates, channel presets or review-platform shortcuts the product ships with
Updates when model behaviour shifts under you
moatNotes: The defensibility is the tuned prompt and the fact that it is already in Portuguese and already on your phone. Neither is a technical moat, both are real friction.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the gap between a paste box and a product is mostly things nobody enjoys building: a layout that works one-handed, prompts that do not produce stiff translated-sounding Portuguese, defaults that are right for the kind of messages you actually get. People paying for this are not paying for intelligence, they are paying to skip the hour of prompt fiddling and the ten minutes of deploying something so their phone can reach it. That is a fine trade for a small monthly fee, and a bad one if you already keep an LLM tab open all day.
notes: The model does the work here, the app just holds the text box. Worth building if only to see how thin the layer is.
prompt:
Build a local-only web app called "Resposta" that drafts replies to messages in Portuguese.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3. No auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud deploy.

Core screen, single page:
- A large textarea for the incoming message.
- A tone selector: formal, neutral, friendly, firm.
- A length selector: short, medium, long.
- A dropdown of saved context presets (see below).
- A "Gerar respostas" button that returns three distinct draft replies, each in its own card with a copy button.

Context presets: a small CRUD panel where I can store named presets, each with a free-text block describing who I am, what the business does, and any rules (for example "never promise refunds", "always sign as Ana"). Presets are stored in SQLite and injected into the system prompt.

API: one route handler, POST /api/draft, calling the OpenAI Chat Completions API with the key from process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY. Stream the response if easy, otherwise plain JSON is fine. Build the system prompt so output is natural Brazilian Portuguese, never translated-sounding, and never explains itself.

History: persist every request and its drafts in SQLite, show the last 50 in a collapsible side list, clicking one reloads the message and drafts.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, billing, email or WhatsApp integrations, mobile apps, multi-language UI, analytics.

Ship: schema created on first run, .env.example with OPENAI_API_KEY, and a README with npm install, npm run dev, and one paragraph on editing the system prompt.
